sections.text: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक्च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत्।
What is called Matter, of what it is composed, whence it came, and why it changes, what the Self is, and what Its power - this I will now briefly set forth.
Seers have sung of It in various ways, in many hymns and sacred Vedic songs, weighty in thought and convincing in argument.

The five great fundamentals (earth, fire, air, water and ether), personality, intellect, the mysterious life force, the ten organs of perception and action, the mind and the five domains of sensation;

We have started discussing chapter 13, Kshetra Kshetrajna Vibhaga yoga, Yoga of knowing the difference between the field and its knower. We are basically learning how to navigate through maya. As we have seen before, we have four great Vedas: Rig, Sama, Yajur, and Atharva.
Each one gave us one great statement which summarizes the entire philosophy of who I am. At the end of the Vedas is a section called Vedanta, literally end of Vedas, which consists of the Upanishads. The Upanishads discuss who we are, what our relationship is to that Almighty, and whether I have an existence before and after my death.
Each one has argued this point logically and came to a logical conclusion about what the truth is, summarized in one great statement in each Veda. So in Rugveda from Ayutary Upanishad, we get Prajnaam brahman. In the end, he says, the real truth is that the consciousness alone is that Almighty, all pervading self.
From this Sama Veda in Chandogya Upanishad came Tattvamasi, that thou art, you are that that which you are seeking as the Supreme Lord is your own self. From the Atharva Veda came I am Atma Brahman. After the inquiry about what the self is, it says, my self is Brahman.
The self which I consider to be myself is Brahman. So that comes from the Atharva Vedas Mandukya Upanishad. The last one is Aham Brahmasmi, I am brahman. The final realization that Brahman is none other than my own self comes from the Yajurveda, from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.
The Gita, as we have seen, is Bhagavan Krishnas collection of all those ideas from the Upanishads, put into one discourse called the Bhagavad Gita. So we have been discussing the Bhagavad Gita, learning the essence of these great statements. Many commentators have said, as we have discussed many times before, that Tattvamasi is the statement which the Gita elaborates upon.
We have learned so far about tat and tvam in the first 12 chapters. For six chapters we learned about tvam, that is, you and I as limited beings. That segment culminated in Dhyana Yoga, Yoga of Meditation.
Once I know who I am as a limited being, now I have to contemplate upon who I am. The next six chapters we discussed about that, that Almighty, the Supreme. What is the nature of that? And that culminated into Bhakti Yoga, Yoga of devotion.
Once I know myself in that Almighty, I will have nothing but devotion for that self. Once I identify with someone, I will be in love with that person. I love something when I know something.
Once I know the nature of the Supreme, then only can I develop devotion for it. So chapter 12 was Bhakti Yoga, Yoga of Devotion. Chapter 13 now connects the two. That thou art -- that correlative verb art is what we are now discussing: how to make the connection between this limited self which I consider to be myself, and that which is the Almighty, all-pervading.
As we have discussed in Self Unfoldment and before, this self which I consider me is a conditioned self, conditioned in my body. And I consider this to be my body. This is a gross body which I consider to be my body which is perceived by everybody else.
Everybody can see how tall I am, how short I am, how old I am. But then there is a subtle body which I am very aware. You may have inkling about it, but you cant perceive it.
Thats my mind and intellect. Thats like a software in this hardware called body. But both of these exist because of the third body, called the causal body, which is the cause for these two to come into existence.
These two cannot come into existence if there is no cause for them. These two came into existence as they are. Why are you not so powerful? Why are you not so smart? Thats because this is what the cause considered the most appropriate form to transact all the desires and vasanas which I have.
So thats the causal body. The causal body is nothing but the leftover tendencies and vasanas from my past experiences. For example, from my past experience of buying a house in this area -- if I made a mistake last time, dont do that again.
Next time when I buy a house, I look for a good school district because thats more important. Lets find which has the best resale value. Dont fall into the trap of this is the most economical area. You need to find something where the resale value is more important.
All these are my past impressions from last time, when I made a mistake. The same way, Bhagavan says that this body and this mind are also ordered by me, custom designed by me. Like when you go online and fill out which color car you want, what shape, what size, what brand, and you put together a customized package.
I heard somewhere that at Starbucks, there are like 5,400 or so different varieties of coffee you can order -- you can customize your coffee. Its the same way I have customized this existence of mine which I call my limited self. Total impressions of my past experiences and tendencies created these two bodies.
Subtle body and gross body. Thats at my micro level. The total tendencies and impressions of all the beings and things in this Jagat, this universe create the total causal body.
And in Sankhya philosophy its called Mola Prakriti. The original nature of this Prakriti, Mula Prakriti. In Vedanta, we call it Maya.
That means ya ma sa maya -- that which is not, but appears to be, that is Maya. These limitations on me -- as my body, my mind, my intellect -- are not actually there. There are no limitations on myself apart from my mind, my intellect, my body.
But it appears to have this limitation. I feel these limitations when I think about myself. Thats because of Maya.
Maya is nothing but my identification with this body, with this mind, with this intellect. As long as that identification is there, all the limitations of my body, mind, and intellect will be there. Once I get out of that identification, those limitations only remain for the body, for the mind, for the intellect -- but not for me.
Vivekananda used to say, I as a monastics have all the problems. But I as I have no problem. I as an architect have all the problems, all limitations. But when I remove all those, the I which remains has no problem because it has no limitation. How to migrate from this limited I and its identification to that unlimited I -- that is what well be discussing from chapter 13 through 18.
And therefore the last chapter, chapter 18, will culminate in Moksha Sannyasa Yoga, Yoga of liberation and renunciation. So we started discussing chapter 13. We have indicated that the very first verse, Arjuna Uvacha, is not in many texts, but it is very appropriate that it was interpolated by some commentator.
Arjuna said, I want to know the nature of these things. What are the things he wants to know? Prakriti -- I want to know the nature of Prakriti. I want to know the nature of Purusha also. In addition, I want to know Kshetra and Kshetrajna -- what is the field and who is the knower of the field.
I want to know what is knowledge and what is to be known. So these are the topics well be discussing going forward. Somebody put it in Arjunas mouth so that we know well be talking about Purusha and Prakriti, Kshetra and Kshetrajna, Jnanam and Jneyam.
If I can differentiate between these two -- what is Kshetra and Kshetrajna, what is Purusha and Prakriti, what is knowledge and what is to be known -- then I have accomplished my task. From the next verse, Bhagavan basically changes the paradigm for us. Up till now, I considered the I to be the knower and the world to be the field of my actions.
So Ive included in the I the knower -- my body, my mind, my intellect is the knower part. Rajan, do you know this? When I say I know it, I mean my mind, my intellect, my body are all included in it. But once I know: Idam Shariram Kaunteya, Kshetram iti abhidhiyate. You want to know what the field is? This body is the field.
One who knows this field is the knower of the field. So this body is the field of activities for the consciousness to function through. It is not I -- this is the field.
In this field, all the activities take place. This field is nothing but part of the Prakriti. I have borrowed from the Prakriti this body.
All the food which I have eaten from the day of my birth till this mornings breakfast is my body. So I actually borrowed from outside. Bhagavan said this is the field.
One who knows this field -- say, I am aware of my body, Im aware my leg is broken -- Im aware Im short, Im aware Im tall. That entity which is aware of the limitations or the qualities of the body, Bhagavan said, is the knower. So he defines what is Kshetra and Kshetrajna. But he included this body in the field.
Body is part of the Prakriti; so is mind; so is intellect. They do not belong to me. They are the equipment borrowed from this Prakriti, and I use them.
Then: Kshetrajnam cha api mam viddhi, sarva-kshetreshu Bharata. I, the knower of this body, am a very distinct individual. You, the knower of your body; she, the knower of her body. Bhagavan says no -- there is only one knower. He knows all the bodies.
All the fields of actions are known by only one entity. Bhagavan says, Thats me. The Kshetrajna is only one. The Kshetra may be many; the fields of activities may be many.
But the knower and the actor is only one. Be clear that Im the only knower in this world. I, the all-pervading self, am the only knower.
Then the next verse, verse 4, says: Tat kshetram yat cha yadrik cha, yad-vikari yatah cha yat, tat samasena me shrinu. Once again he told us what we are going to discuss, then well discuss it, and in the end well say, This is what we discussed. So this is what were going to discuss: What is the field and what is its nature? What are its modifications? Because sometimes we dont recognize the thing which gets modified. We may know its in a raw form but when modified we dont recognize.
So you should also know the modification of Bhagavan and when it is and also who it is and what his powers are. So he basically said well be discussing this. What is the nature of the field? What are its modifications, where it is, how it functions, what are the fields powers? So we are talking about Maya -- what Mayas powers are, how it deludes you into thinking you are what you are not.
Bhagavan said, Ill be telling you briefly, so please listen. Rishibhih bahudha gitam, chandobhih vividhaih prithak, Brahma-sutra-padaih cha eva, hetumadbhih vinishchitaih. Even Bhagavan Krishna says, I cannot say that this is my own idea. In our culture, there is nothing called an original idea. Even Bhagavan cannot say, This is my idea. It has to be validated by many seers before you, and many people must have attested that this is the truth.
Then only is that truth validated. Ours is a Veda-bound culture. We have to have proof in the Vedas for the idea which we are propagating or promoting.
Has to have proof in Vedas. So Bhagavan Krishna said, Im not going to tell you anything new. Rishibhih bahudha gitam -- the seers before me have already sung this truth in many ways.

These verses enumerate the 24 constituents of the field: the five great elements (earth, water, fire, air, ether), the ego (ahamkara), intellect (buddhi), the unmanifest (avyaktam), the ten sense organs, the mind, and the five sense objects. Krishna emphasizes that this teaching is not new - it has been sung by seers in various hymns and validated through the Brahma Sutras. Today, take inventory of what you normally consider yourself. Your physical body made of elements, your sense of individual identity, your reasoning faculty, your perceptions - all these belong to the field, not to the Knower.
Reflect on how you have customized your existence through past impressions and tendencies (vasanas). Like ordering a custom car with specific features, your body, mind, and intellect have been shaped by accumulated experiences. This is not cause for guilt but for understanding - these are borrowed equipment from Prakriti. The question becomes: if all this is borrowed, who is the borrower? Spend time today noticing how you identify with your personality traits, your intellectual capabilities, your physical characteristics. Can you see them as equipment rather than essence?
As a daily practice, when you wake up tomorrow, before getting out of bed, mentally list the components of your field: your body lying there, your mind starting to generate thoughts, your intellect planning the day. Then ask: Who is aware of this entire field awakening? Rest in that awareness for a moment before beginning your day.
